items.answer:
Here’s the expected approach for a sensitive workplace complaint (e.g., harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats, violence) and any related HR case:

- Treat it as a “Sensitive workplace issue” and handle under the Workplace Conduct Policy [HR-POL-011 §3.4].
- Prioritize safety first. If there is any immediate risk, direct the person to emergency support before any administrative steps [HR-POL-011 §8].
- Do not investigate or decide the facts. Provide guidance and route the concern to People and Culture/HR; the assistant must not adjudicate sensitive issues [HR-POL-011 §8; HR-POL-011 §9.1].
- Escalate through the formal channel. Concerns involving harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats, or significant security risk must go to the appropriate HR/People and Culture channel [HR-POL-001 §4.2; HR-POL-011 §8].
- Maintain confidentiality and use only authorized systems and channels when handling any details of the case [HR-POL-001 §4.2].
- Reinforce non-retaliation. Managers must avoid retaliation or perceived retaliation, and workers who raise concerns in good faith must not be retaliated against [HR-POL-011 §8; HR-POL-011 §4.2].
- Provide clear next steps. Explain how to submit the report (e.g., HR/People and Culture intake) and what information is typically needed to open a case, without soliciting unnecessary details; share information only with those who need to know per policy [HR-POL-001 §4.2].

If any required policy detail is missing for the specific situation, inform the person that the assistant cannot determine outcomes and recommend direct escalation to HR/People and Culture.

Managers must maintain appropriate professional boundaries and must avoid retaliation or perceived retaliation.

Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on their recorded full-time-equivalent fraction.

A change in scheduled hours applies prospectively and must not be used to retrospectively recalculate leave already taken.

Available programs may include health support, wellbeing services, professional development, and other company-approved benefits.

A benefit description does not create an entitlement beyond the recorded eligibility and election.
sources.title: Employee Benefits Policy

sources.snippet:
Full-time employees receive 20 days of paid time off each year.

Entitlement accrues progressively across the year and is recorded in the employee's paid-time-off balance.

An employee must not represent projected future accrual as currently available leave unless the manager and People and Culture approve an advance arrangement.

sources.snippet:
Employees should begin with the policy whose title most closely matches the request. A paid-time-off question belongs in the Paid Time Off Policy, while an unplanned health-related absence belongs in the Leave and Absence Policy. Where a request spans more than one policy, the response should identify the role of each document instead of blending their rules into one unsupported summary.

A policy title, section heading, and supporting passage should accompany each material policy claim. This approach allows the employee to distinguish an authoritative rule from general guidance, an example, or a suggested next step. A citation must not be attached to a claim that the cited passage does not actually support.

sources.snippet:
Personal and carer's leave requests should be reported as soon as practicable and no later than the employee's scheduled start time where possible.

If the employee is unable to notify the manager, another person may make initial contact, followed by the employee when practicable.

sources.snippet:
- Urgent personal circumstances may prevent 10 calendar days of notice; the employee should notify the manager as soon as practicable.
- An advance against future accrual requires documented approval from the manager and People and Culture.
- Extended leave, unpaid leave, and personal or carer's leave are governed by HR-POL-010.

An absence must be recorded under the category that best reflects the circumstances.

Paid time off must not be used to obscure a personal, carer's, or other leave event where a different policy process applies.

- If the matter includes sensitive medical information, escalate rather than adjudicate.
